Therefore, the gods are the princes of all species, and they are followed by the gods whose prince is <term>ousia</term> <gloss>essence</gloss>. These sensible ones are of both origins and are similar to them, they who complete all things through sensible nature, each one illuminating its own work through the other. The heaven, or whatever is understood by that name, its <term>ousiarches</term> <gloss>ruler of essence</gloss> is Jupiter; for through the heaven, Jupiter provides life to all things. The <term>ousiarches</term> of the sun is light, for the good of light is poured into us through the orb of the sun. Of the thirty-six stars fixed forever in the same place (whose name is Horoscopes), their <term>ousiarches</term> or prince is he whom they call <term>Pantomorphon</term> <gloss>all-formed</gloss>, who creates diverse forms for diverse species. The seven spheres which are called erratic have <term>ousiarchas</term> <gloss>rulers of essence</gloss>, that is, their own princes, whom they call fortune, <term>heimarmene</term> <gloss>fate</gloss>, by which all things are changed, with the firmest stability of the law of nature and varied by everlasting agitation. But the air is the organ, or machine, of all things, through which all things come to be. Moreover, the second <term>ousiarches</term> of this belongs to mortals, and things similar to them. Therefore, with these things standing thus, moving from the lowest to the highest, all things naturally pertaining to themselves are so connected that mortal things are annexed to mortals, and sensible things to sensible things. Indeed, the summit of government obeys that highest lord, so that they are not many, or rather, they are one; for all things hang from one, and flow down rather from it, though when they are distant they are believed to be many things separately. But when unified, they are one, or rather two: that from which all things are made, and that by which they are made. That is, the matter from which they are made, and the will of Him by whose nod other things are effected. ASCLE. Is this reason again thus, O Trismegistus? TRISME. Such it is, O Asclepius. <summary>This passage details the celestial hierarchy and the divine governance of the cosmos, identifying the rulers of essence (ousiarches) for the heavens, the sun, and the stars, and explaining how all created things originate from divine will and primordial matter.</summary>
